subject: Reserved QPS pressure: urgent exec action requested
messages:
From: Anna Lin <anna.lin@blueharbor.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Elevated latency + 5xx — reserved capacity shortfall

Hi Grace / David,

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx rates and tail latency against our reserved endpoint (model: rwd-large-v2) at ~08:30 PDT this morning. Our downstream job processors are queueing and failing — we’ve had multiple retries and one customer-facing batch job timed out.

Attached is a small trace and a sample of request IDs showing high queue_time (~450ms p50 -> 2s p99) and elevated token-queuing. BlueHarbor is currently on a reserved commit (monthly) and this is directly affecting our SLA.

Can you confirm whether this is an isolated dedicated GPU pool saturation event or a routing/regional fallback? We need ETA on mitigation and any remediation plan. We’re also starting procurement conversations internally to explore redundancy options if this will be recurring.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Lin
Head of Platform Engineering, BlueHarbor
anna.lin@blueharbor.com

Attachment: sample-trace.json (JSON trace excerpt, 6KB)

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lin <anna.lin@blueharbor.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency + 5xx — reserved capacity shortfall

Anna — thanks for the quick heads up and the trace. I’m escalating immediately.

Short answers up front: 1) we see a sharp spike in token queue depth on the dedicated pool servicing your reservation; 2) routing fallback did not trigger — requests are hitting the reserved capacity directly; 3) we are standing up an ops bridge now and will propose short-term mitigations + a follow-up plan within 60 minutes.

Marcus, David — can you join the bridge and confirm whether we can authorize emergency burst capacity for BlueHarbor and whether a cache warm/prefix purge would help reduce p99s quickly?

Naomi — flagging for CS communication and possible credit discussion depending on impact window.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachment: none

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lin <anna.lin@blueharbor.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency + 5xx — reserved capacity shortfall

On Wed, Aug 5, 2026 at 9:35 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus, David — can you join the bridge and confirm whether we can authorize emergency burst capacity for BlueHarbor and whether a cache warm/prefix purge would help reduce p99s quickly?

Joining now — quick technical summary from the infra side: we’re observing a combination of (A) sustained high sequence lengths from their job processors, (B) a KV-cache miss storm for a recent model rollout they adopted (rwd-large-v2, ~2026-08-01), and (C) a transient imbalance where one shard of the dedicated pool hit cushion limits while others still have headroom.

Immediate actions taken (in progress):
- Enabled emergency burst authorization on the dedicated pool (temporary, up to +18% capacity) to relieve queueing.
- Pushed a targeted KV-cache pre-warm for BlueHarbor’s hot prefixes (reduces cold-attention re-compute).
- Rebalanced a noisy tenant from the hot shard to an adjacent shard — this should reduce the p99 within ~10min.

We need an ops run for a memory-defragmentation step on the affected hosts; that will require a short rolling restart per host (we will limit impact and coordinate with customer). I’ll keep Anna updated on expected p99 reduction.

Attachment: pool-metrics.png (grafana snapshot)

Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Anna Lin <anna.lin@blueharbor.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency + 5xx — reserved capacity shortfall

Thanks Marcus — we can see the p99 tail coming down in our graphs (app metrics). The burst appears to reduce queue_time, but one of our batch pipelines still sees intermittent retries. We’re OK with a short rolling restart as long as there’s coordination on the window (we have peak jobs at 13:00 PDT).

Can you confirm the duration of the burst window and whether logs will be preserved for our audit? Also, can the team estimate potential financial exposure for burst usage (we’re on a committed plan of fixed monthly units)? We’ll need that for our procurement discussion.

Anna

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Anna Lin <anna.lin@blueharbor.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Elevated latency + 5xx — reserved capacity shortfall

Hi Anna — appreciate the patience. Our recommended customer-facing communication: short status update now, notice before any rolling restarts, and a post-incident summary with root cause and timeline.

On credits: when a reserved commitment is impacted by platform-side saturation we typically offer a restorative credit tied to the impacted window. Preliminary estimate (working from Marcus's telemetry): 20–30% of last week’s committed units would be an appropriate one-time restoration pending final post-incident analysis. I’ve attached a working sheet; want to confirm if BlueHarbor would accept a credit vs. an immediate billing adjustment.

Grace — this needs an approval from finance/ops (and a short note to the leadership team because this could set a precedent if we see repeated events).

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success Operations — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Attachment: credit-calculation.xlsx

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency + 5xx — reserved capacity shortfall

Thanks for the thread and the rapid response team. I’ve reviewed the initial telemetry and Marcus’s mitigations. Approve the following immediate actions:

- Confirm emergency burst reconciliation: allow the burst authorization for BlueHarbor for the 6-hour window we used (ops to record exact token/compute usage).
- Approve a one-time restorative credit up to 25% of last month’s committed units pending RCA. Finance to finalize exact $ amount; Naomi please start the credit ticket.
- Notify the SLT (execs) with a 1–pager describing root cause, mitigation steps, and recommended systemic fixes (shard rebalancer tuning + improved KV-cache warm on deploys).

Marcus/David — prioritize a postmortem and an action item to add automatic shard fallback logic to prevent single-shard cushion exhaustion.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Operations — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

On the customer communication — Naomi, please send the status update and the restart window to Anna and copy legal/contracts (contract-admin@blueharbor.com).
